answer: Each identity claims one orchard row, locks a 70-credit bond, and files a signed saffron tally. A copper tag is fixed to the batch and logged once in the registry. An auditor weighs the batch against the yield table and checks the serial; a shortfall over 3 percent or a reused serial burns the bond. Fees start at 34 credits, rise by 6 per extra identity, so the thousandth costs 6028 and 1000 fakes pay 3,031,000 plus 70,000 locked. Rented tags fail because one serial serves one row and one batch cannot cover two tallies. An honest grower pays 34 once and recovers the 70 bond after audit.
